original.subject: Turn one browser procedure into a guide
original.preview_text: Walk through the steps in a web app, then share the how-to with your team.
original.headline: Capture the process as you perform it
original.body:
If a useful IT procedure lives in one person’s head, capture it while they perform it in a web app.

Scribe is documentation and workflow-capture software. On the **free Basic plan**, you walk through a browser-based software setup or account configuration, and Scribe turns those steps into a how-to guide.

Share the finished guide with your team so someone else can follow the procedure instead of reconstructing it from memory.

Basic covers procedures performed in the browser. Capturing desktop-application procedures requires a Pro or Enterprise account.

You can test that first browser procedure without paying for a plan.

issues.detail: "Preview text: Walk through the steps in a web app, then share the how-to with your team.": The sources support use with web apps, guide generation, and sharing by link or embed. They do not literally establish that Basic creates the guide specifically by recording the steps as the user walks through them.
"Capture the process as you perform it": The supplied excerpts mention automatic capture and web-process capture generally, but do not clearly entail this as-you-perform mechanism on the Basic plan.

"If a useful IT procedure lives in one person’s head, capture it while they perform it in a web app.": The undocumented-procedure situation is appropriately conditional and web-app operation is supported, but the sources do not explicitly establish that Basic captures the procedure while it is being performed.

"On the free Basic plan, you walk through a browser-based software setup or account configuration, and Scribe turns those steps into a how-to guide.": Basic is free, works in the browser, and generates how-to guides. The literal evidence does not establish the claimed causal mechanism that walking through the setup or configuration causes Scribe to turn those performed steps into the guide.

"Document one browser procedure →": Together with “Free Basic Plan” and the paragraph claiming that walking through steps creates the guide, this CTA implies that the free Basic route provides the as-performed capture workflow. Browser guide generation is supported, but that specific mechanism is not established by the literal evidence.

The supplied quotations establish free Basic browser use and guide generation, but not that Basic records a walkthrough and converts the performed steps into the guide. This unresolved mechanism also affects the preview, heading, conditional opening, and CTA’s implied offer.

reads.what_it_sells: Scribe offers software that records me completing a browser-based IT procedure and turns the captured steps into a guide my team can reuse, with one procedure testable on its free Basic plan.
reads.biggest_doubt: I would hesitate to run capture software through a software setup or account configuration without knowing what browser data it records, where that data goes, and whether credentials or other sensitive information can be excluded before sharing.
fixes: Rewrite "On the free Basic plan, you walk through a browser-based software setup or account configuration, and Scribe turns those steps into a how-to guide." to explain what is actually captured and whether sensitive information can be excluded.
Expand "Share the finished guide with your team" to state whether I can review, edit, or redact the generated steps before anyone else sees them.

email.preview_text: Generate and share a guide for one routine IT procedure with Scribe Basic.
email.headline: Give your team a procedure to follow
email.body:
Pick one routine IT procedure completed in a web app. For this first test, choose one that does not expose credentials or sensitive records.

Scribe is documentation and workflow-capture software. Its free Basic plan works in the browser and generates a how-to guide you can share with your team, giving them a procedure to follow instead of reconstructing it from memory.

Keep the test focused on one browser-based procedure. Basic is free, so you can see the guide it generates before deciding whether Scribe fits this kind of IT documentation.

Desktop-application capture requires Pro or Enterprise. For this free first use, stay in a web app and create the guide with Basic.

decision.summary: The implied access route is Scribe's free Basic plan. Across the subject, body, and CTA, the draft implies that the reader can perform a procedure in a web app, generate a how-to guide, and share it with the team through that route. Those Basic entitlements are supported, and the draft correctly reserves desktop-application capture for Pro or Enterprise. No material unsupported assertion or instruction violation was found.

benefit_retention.explanation: The revision retains the supported action and payoff: use free Basic to turn one browser-based procedure into a shareable guide that teammates can follow instead of reconstructing the procedure from memory. It also preserves the material desktop limitation.

reads.what_it_sells: Scribe offers free browser-based workflow-capture software that generates shareable how-to guides for routine IT procedures, potentially reducing the time I spend documenting steps for colleagues.
reads.relevance_feedback: The offer is relevant to an IT team responsible for internal support documentation, but the profile only presents undocumented knowledge as an inferred market observation with uncertain current applicability. The email additionally assumes I have a browser-based procedure that colleagues reconstruct from memory; that may be plausible, but it is not established as my situation.
assumed_experiences: Profile-supported: I am part of the selected audience of IT teams.
Inferred context, not established biography: I may be responsible for internal support documentation.
Email-only: I have a routine browser-based IT procedure worth documenting.
Email-only: my team currently reconstructs at least one procedure from memory.
Email-only: I can test capture without exposing credentials or sensitive records.
reads.problem_now: Avoiding undocumented procedural knowledge is relevant to IT work, but whether it is a current problem for me, and whether a browser-only procedure is the useful place to address it, remains unknown. No immediate deadline or active documentation project is established.
reads.biggest_doubt: I cannot picture what the test actually involves: whether I install something, what Scribe captures while I perform the procedure, what the generated guide contains, or how it is shared and controlled. That uncertainty matters for an IT tool handling internal workflows, even during a limited nonsensitive test.
reads.to_click_it_would_have_to: I would have clicked if this email had told me exactly how the browser capture works, what I would need to install or authorize, and what shareable output the first test produces.
fixes: Rewrite "Scribe is documentation and workflow-capture software" to explain the actual capture operation: whether Basic requires an extension, what it records, and what guide elements it generates.
Replace the repeated instruction "Keep the test focused on one browser-based procedure" with a short description of the test sequence, from starting capture through reviewing and sharing the guide.
Expand "a how-to guide you can share with your team" to state what sharing means and what access controls, if any, apply; the current line leaves the practical result unclear.

Condense "Desktop-application capture requires Pro or Enterprise. For this free first use, stay in a web app and create the guide with Basic." The browser-only limitation is already clear and takes space that could explain the first-use workflow.
reads.material_revision: Explain the missing operation between choosing a procedure and receiving a guide. I still cannot picture what I install or authorize, what is captured as I work, how I review the generated steps, or how teammates receive the result. Those details should replace the repeated browser-only limitation without claiming capabilities the email has not established.
